chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn 'Abdus, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who made a vow to Allah to fast for a year but was unable to, he said: 'He fasts for one month and part of the other month.' Then he said: 'There is no harm in interrupting the fasting.'

key_terms.نَذْرًا: Vow (a voluntary commitment to perform an act of worship)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for fulfilling a vow to fast for a year if one cannot fast continuously?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexibility in fulfilling a vow of continuous annual fasting, permitting the obligation to be discharged by fasting one full month plus part of another. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle of ease (*taysir*) in vows, allowing for interruptions due to valid excuses without nullifying the vow's core requirement. The permissibility of breaking the fast underscores the distinction between the vow's binding nature and the practical conditions of its execution.
